name: ADC0832
full_name: 8-Bit Serial I/O A/D Converter with 2-Channel Multiplexer
description: 8-bit successive-approximation A/D converter with a serial I/O compliant with TI's MICROWIRE standard for direct interface to COPS-family processors, and easily bit-banged from any microprocessor or shift register. The ADC0832 is the 2-channel-mux member of the ADC0831/2/4/8 family (0831 is a fixed single differential channel with no address pin; 0834 adds a 4-channel mux; 0838 an 8-channel mux). Unlike the ADC0831, the ADC0832 has a DI (data in / mux address) pin: after CS goes low, the host clocks in a start bit followed by SGL/DIF and ODD/SIGN address bits on DI to select CH0 or CH1 as single-ended inputs, or CH0/CH1 as a differential pair (with selectable polarity), before the conversion result is clocked out on DO. Originally a National Semiconductor design, continued by TI (National's ADC family retains the '-N' suffix post-acquisition). Operates ratiometrically from a single 5V supply or with an external VREF to encode a smaller analog span across the full 8 bits; needs no zero or full-scale adjustment.

pins.name: CS
pins.description: chip select, active low; must be low to enable CLK/DI and start/continue a conversion, high tri-states DO

pins.name: CH0
pins.description: analog input channel 0; usable single-ended or, paired with CH1, as one side of a differential input depending on the SGL/DIF and ODD/SIGN bits clocked in on DI

pins.name: CH1
pins.description: analog input channel 1; usable single-ended or, paired with CH0, as the other side of a differential input depending on the SGL/DIF and ODD/SIGN bits clocked in on DI

pins.name: GND
pins.description: ground reference for both analog and digital sections; also the internal COM node used for single-ended conversions

pins.name: DI
pins.description: serial data/mux-address input; after CS falls, clocks in the start bit, then SGL/DIF (1=single-ended, 0=differential) and ODD/SIGN (selects CH0 vs CH1, or polarity of the CH0/CH1 differential pair) to configure the mux before conversion; don't-care once the mux is set until the next conversion cycle

pins.name: DO
pins.description: serial data output, tri-state; after the MUX settling time, shifts out the conversion result MSB-first then re-shifts it LSB-first on CLK edges, tri-states when CS goes high

pins.name: CLK
pins.description: external clock input; also times the successive-approximation conversion (10 kHz min to 400 kHz design limit, 40-60% duty cycle)

pins.name: VCC (VREF)
pins.description: positive supply, 4.5V to 6.3V operating (6.5V absolute max); pin is internally tied to VREF, so this single pin also sets the ratiometric full-scale (256-code) span -- there is no separate VREF pin on this package

PDIP-8.notes: Per TI datasheet SNAS531B (Aug 1999, rev March 2013), Figure 5 'ADC0832-N 2-Channel MUX PDIP Package (P) Top View', page 2. Figure notes: 'COM internally connected to GND. extra.input configuration: 2-channel mux (CH0, CH1), software-configured via DI for single-ended or differential (with selectable polarity) operation
extra.mux addressing protocol: with CS low, clock in on DI: start bit (must be 1), then SGL/DIF (1=single-ended, 0=differential), then ODD/SIGN (single-ended: 0=CH0, 1=CH1; differential: selects which of CH0/CH1 is + vs -); DI is don't-care after mux settling until the next conversion
extra.total unadjusted error: +-1/2 LSB (B-grade, e.g. ADC0832BCIWM) or +-1 LSB (C-grade, e.g. ADC0832CCIWM), tested at VREF=5.00V
extra.conversion time: 32us typ, tC = 8 clock periods (not including CS setup/MUX addressing time) at fCLK=250kHz
extra.clock frequency: 10kHz min to 400kHz design limit; specs given typ at fCLK=250kHz
extra.clock duty cycle: 40% to 60% (clock may be stopped low indefinitely if analog input is stable, or high up to 60us max)
extra.ICC supply current: 2.3mA typ, 6.5mA max (includes ladder/mux current, VCC=5V, fCLK=250kHz, CS=1) -- notably higher than the fixed-channel ADC0831/0834/0838 (0.9mA typ/2.5mA max) because of the resistor ladder mux
extra.input voltage range: 0V to 5V with single 5V supply; VIN(-) staying within ~50mV of the rails avoids input-protection-diode conduction (needs VCC >= 4.95V for a true full 0-5V span)
extra.output data order: MSB-first, then LSB-first re-shift on the same DO transmission (unlike the ADC0831 which outputs MSB-first only)

typical_application: Low-cost 8-bit data acquisition of one or two analog channels (single-ended or differential) over a simple CS/CLK/DI/DO serial interface compatible with TI MICROWIRE and easily bit-banged by any microprocessor; typical uses include reading two single-ended potentiometer/sensor channels from one part, or a differential bridge/pressure sensor with software-selectable polarity, feeding a COPS or general-purpose MCU.
gotchas: the -N suffix (ADC0831-N/0832-N/0834-N/0838-N) marks TI's continuation of the original National Semiconductor ADC0831 family after the 2011 acquisition; it is not TI's usual NRND marker

ADC0832 is the only member of the family with a plain 8-pin PDIP that also carries a 14-pin SOIC option (NPA) sharing the ADC0834's mechanical footprint with 6 NC pins -- do not assume all 14 legs on the SOIC part are active

unlike the ADC0831 (no DI pin, fixed single differential channel), the ADC0832 needs 3 address bits (start, SGL/DIF, ODD/SIGN) clocked in on DI before the conversion result appears -- get the address bit order wrong and you'll read the wrong channel or wrong polarity, not just garbage data

VCC and VREF are the same physical pin on the ADC0832 package (unlike the ADC0834-N/0838-N which break out a separate VREF) -- you cannot use an external reference below VCC without also dropping the supply rail

DO shifts out MSB-first immediately, then re-shifts the same result LSB-first afterward; a receiver expecting only one bit order will misread half the transmission if it doesn't stop clocking after 8 bits
ICC is notably higher than the fixed-channel siblings (2.3mA typ vs 0.9mA typ) because the mux resistor ladder draws current whenever CS is low -- factor this into low-power designs

VIN(-) must stay close to GND (within ~50mV) or its internal protection diode conducts and corrupts the conversion; a true 0V-5V single-supply input range requires VCC >= 4.95V to keep enough diode margin

the 6.3-8.5V internal zener/shunt-regulator trick for running from higher supply voltages needs the separate V+ pin, which the PDIP-8/SOIC-14 ADC0832 package does not break out (only VCC) -- that trick applies to the ADC0834-N/0838-N packages that do expose V+
